Zory Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żory, Poland

Not demolished. Żory's Jewish presence dates to the beginning of the 16th century, though all Jews were expelled in 1565 under German imperial rule and only returned after 1713; the community reached 542 people (13.5 percent) by 1846. This cemetery, established in 1814 after Żory's Jews had previously been buried in Mikołów, documented elsewhere in this collection, holds the tombstone of Rabbi Nachman Wolff Wischnitz, who died in 1823 as the result of a fire. During WWII, the funeral house was destroyed in January 1945 fighting and later demolished in the 1960s; the site was used afterward as a playing field. In May 1940, the Germans deported all of Żory's Jews to the Będzin Ghetto.
